stepTitle: Identify the point on the unit circle corresponding to $$\theta=\frac{5\pi}{4}.$$ \n Note that the point A is $$\frac{1}{8}$$ around the circle in the counterclockwise direction measured from the positive horizontal axis; B is $$\frac{1}{4}$$ C is $$\frac{5}{8}$$ D is $$\frac{7}{8}$$.

figureAlts.figure1.gif: A unit circle has 4 points along its circumference. Point A is located on the circle halfway between the horizontal and vertical, with both coordinates positive (first quadrant). Point B is located where the circle intersects the vertical axis in the positive (upward) direction. Point C is located on the circle halfway between the horizontal and vertical, with negative coordinates (third quadrant). Point D is located on the circle halfway between the horizontal and vertical, with a positive horizontal coordinate and a negative vertical coordinate (fourth quadrant).
